security_audit.summary: The Ruby backtick detections are false positives from Markdown code fences in SKILL.md. The only confirmed risks are low severity examples that make outbound HTTP requests to httpbin.org and py-spy commands that attach to a user-specified process. No evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Use a local test server or mock endpoint, and tell users before any example performs outbound requests.

remediation.issue: py-spy examples attach to a running process by PID.
remediation.suggestion: State that profiling must target only authorized processes and may expose stack frames or arguments.

content.value_statement: Slow Python code can hide bottlenecks across CPU, memory, I/O, and database work. This skill guides profiling, benchmarking, and targeted optimization with practical Python examples.
actual_capabilities: Shows CPU profiling with cProfile and pstats.
Shows line and memory profiling with line_profiler and memory_profiler.
Explains py-spy commands for live Python process profiling.
Compares common optimization patterns using timeit benchmarks.
Covers async I/O, multiprocessing, NumPy, caching, and database batching.
limitations: It provides examples and guidance, not an automated optimizer.
Benchmark results depend on hardware, Python version, and workload.
Some tools require separate installation and local permissions.
Network examples contact a public demo endpoint if executed.

use_cases.title: Diagnose API Latency
use_cases.description: Profile slow Python request paths, identify hot functions, and select targeted code or data structure improvements.

use_cases.title: Optimize Data Pipelines
use_cases.description: Reduce memory pressure and runtime in Python data processing with generators, batching, caching, and NumPy guidance.

use_cases.title: Profile Live Services
use_cases.description: Use py-spy and measurement practices to inspect authorized production Python processes with lower disruption.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python function and suggest the simplest profiling approach before optimization.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Optimizations
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me benchmark two Python implementations and explain which metrics should guide the final choice.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Memory Use
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Python workflow for memory pressure and suggest generator, iterator, cache, or object-layout improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Profiling
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe profiling plan for an authorized Python service with CPU, memory, I/O, and database checks.

output_examples.input: A Python endpoint is slow, but the cause is unknown.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend measuring first, running cProfile, sorting cumulative time, and focusing changes on the hottest functions.

output_examples.input: A script loads a large file before processing it.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest iterator-based processing, memory snapshots, and a benchmark comparing peak memory and runtime.

output_examples.input: A database import commits every inserted row.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend batching writes, using a single transaction, and measuring throughput before and after the change.

best_practices: Profile before changing code so work targets measured bottlenecks.
Benchmark each change with representative inputs and stable conditions.
Optimize hot paths while keeping code readable and maintainable.
anti_patterns: Optimizing rare code paths before measuring user-visible impact.
Comparing benchmark results from different environments without noting context.
Running live-process profiling without authorization or operational safeguards.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically optimize my code?
faq.answer: No. It provides profiling methods, examples, and optimization patterns that guide manual changes.

faq.question: Which profiler should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with cProfile for CPU time, then use line or memory tools when you need more detail.

faq.question: Can it help with memory leaks?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows memory profiling, tracemalloc snapshots, garbage collection checks, and memory-efficient data patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover production profiling?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes py-spy examples for authorized live Python processes with low application overhead.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Are the example results guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on workload, hardware, Python version, dependencies, and benchmark setup.
